subject: astronomy
title: Solar Calculations
welcome_lead: Calculate solar wind travel times, Sun-Earth distances and flare speeds.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy calculations: solar wind speed, light travel and sunspot cycles.
final_note: Quantitative work shows how connected Earth and Sun really are.

concepts.def: Charged particles flowing outwards at ~400-800 km/s.
Bubble of solar wind extending past Pluto.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1 AU ~ 1.5 x 10^8 km. At 400 km/s the wind takes 1.5 x 10^8 / 400 = 3.75 x 10^5 s ~ 4.3 days to reach Earth. Faster CMEs can take less than a day.
Light travels at 3 x 10^5 km/s, so it covers 1.5 x 10^8 km in 1.5 x 10^8 / 3 x 10^5 = 500 s = 8.3 minutes. You always see the Sun as it was ~8 minutes ago.
Sunspot counts peak every ~11 years. The magnetic polarity reverses each cycle, so the full magnetic cycle is ~22 years.
